stages.title: Scene graph -> world matrices
stages.caption: The camp is a tree of nodes. Each leaf draws one unit primitive (cube, sphere, cylinder, cone); its world matrix is the product of the local translate-rotate-scale matrices from the root down to it. Colours = composite objects.
stages.formula: M_world = M_parent * T * R * S          p_world = M_world * p_model
stages.concepts: hierarchical modelling, affine transforms, homogeneous coordinates

stages.title: Vertex transform: model -> world -> view -> clip -> NDC -> pixels
stages.caption: Every vertex is moved into the camera's frame (view matrix), projected (clip space), clipped against the view frustum (-w <= x, y, z <= w), divided by w (perspective divide) into normalised device coordinates and mapped to pixels.
stages.formula: p_clip = P * V * M * p     ndc = p_clip.xyz / p_clip.w     x_px = (ndc.x + 1) / 2 * W
stages.concepts: view frustum, perspective projection, clipping, viewport transform

stages.title: Primitive assembly + back-face culling
stages.caption: The index buffer groups vertices into triangles. A triangle whose projected corners wind clockwise shows its back to the camera and is dropped before rasterisation: about half of every closed mesh is never shaded.
stages.formula: 2A = sum_i (x_i * y_i+1 - x_i+1 * y_i)      A > 0: counter-clockwise = front      A < 0: culled
stages.concepts: indexed meshes, winding order, signed area

stages.title: Rasterisation: coverage, edge functions, barycentrics
stages.caption: For each pixel centre p the three edge functions are evaluated. p is covered when all three agree in sign (the top-left rule settles shared edges). Divided by the triangle's area they are the barycentric weights w0, w1, w2.
stages.concepts: scan conversion, edge functions, barycentric coordinates

stages.title: Colour interpolation: affine vs perspective-correct, Gouraud vs Phong
stages.caption: Vertex attributes are blended with the barycentric weights. Blending in screen space (affine) bends patterns on surfaces seen at an angle; dividing by w first keeps them straight. Gouraud lights the vertices and blends colours; Phong blends normals and lights every pixel.
stages.formula: affine: a = sum w_i a_i        perspective-correct: a = sum(w_i a_i / w_clip_i) / sum(w_i / w_clip_i)
stages.concepts: attribute interpolation, perspective-correct mapping, shading models

stages.title: Depth test: the Z-buffer and overdraw
stages.caption: Every fragment's depth is compared with the depth already stored for its pixel: nearer wins, the rest is discarded. Depth is stored non-linearly (precision near the camera). The heat map counts fragments per pixel: all but one were wasted.
stages.formula: pass if z_frag < z_buffer        z_ndc = (f + n) / (f - n) - 2 f n / ((f - n) d)

stages.title: Surface buffers (G-buffer)
stages.caption: The attributes lighting needs, stored per pixel: albedo (base colour), world normal, roughness / metalness and depth. The screen-space passes (SSAO, reflections, fog) read these images instead of the geometry.
stages.formula: normal stored as n * 0.5 + 0.5        P_world = (V P)^-1 * (2 uv - 1, 2 d - 1, 1), then / w
stages.concepts: deferred data, encoding vectors in textures, reconstruction from depth

stages.title: Shadow map: the scene seen from the light
stages.caption: The scene is drawn once more from the moon / sun into a depth texture. A pixel is in shadow when its light-space depth is farther than what the light saw there; percentage-closer filtering (PCF) averages many such tests into a soft edge.
stages.formula: lit(p) = 1/N * sum_k [ z_light(p) - bias <= shadowMap(uv_light(p) + o_k) ]
stages.concepts: two-pass rendering, light space, depth comparison, filtering

stages.title: Lighting: ambient + diffuse + specular
stages.caption: The key light split into its terms: ambient (sky fill), diffuse (Lambert, N.L) and specular (Blinn-Phong highlight around the half vector H). The renderer itself uses the physically based version: GGX, Smith geometry, Schlick Fresnel.
stages.formula: I = k_a A + k_d (N.L) C s + k_s (N.H)^n C s       H = normalize(L + V),  s = shadow
stages.concepts: local illumination, Lambert's cosine law, Blinn-Phong, PBR

stages.title: Reflection: mirror law and screen-space ray marching
stages.caption: The reflected ray leaves at the angle it arrived (mirror law). Screen-space reflections march that ray through the depth buffer until it slips behind a surface, then reuse the colour already on screen there, weighted by Fresnel.

stages.title: Screen-space ambient occlusion
stages.caption: Points are sampled in a hemisphere around each pixel's normal; those that end up behind the depth buffer are occluded. Creases, corners and contact areas receive less sky light.
stages.formula: AO = 1 - 1/N * sum_i [ depth(s_i) closer than s_i ] * range(s_i)
stages.concepts: Monte Carlo sampling, hemisphere integration, screen-space approximation

stages.title: Fog and volumetric light
stages.caption: Light scattered by the air is integrated along each view ray (marching through the shadow map gives light shafts). The surface colour is dimmed by the transmittance and the in-scattered light is added.
stages.formula: T = exp(-sigma d)        L = L_surface * T + L_inscatter
stages.concepts: participating media, Beer-Lambert law, ray marching

stages.title: Bloom: threshold, mip chain, blur
stages.caption: Pixels brighter than a threshold leak light around them, like a real lens. The bright part is extracted, halved again and again with a 13-tap filter (a cheap wide blur), then the chain is upsampled with a 3x3 tent and added back.
stages.formula: b = max(0, max(r,g,b) - T) (soft knee)     mip_k+1 = down13(mip_k)     bloom = sum_k tent(mip_k)
stages.concepts: image pyramids, separable / multi-scale blur, thresholding

stages.title: Tone mapping + exposure
stages.caption: The HDR image spans many stops of brightness. Exposure (auto: from the mean log luminance) scales it, the ACES filmic curve compresses the highlights smoothly and the sRGB curve encodes it for the display.
stages.formula: e = e0 * 2^(key - mean log2 L)       c = ACES(1.6 e L)        out = sRGB(c)
stages.concepts: dynamic range, exposure, tone curves, gamma encoding

stages.title: Temporal anti-aliasing
stages.caption: Every frame the projection moves by a sub-pixel Halton (2,3) offset. The history (reprojected, clipped to the current neighbourhood) is blended with the new frame: edges converge to a supersampled result over ~8 frames.
stages.formula: h_t = lerp(c_t, clip(h_t-1), 0.9)        jitter_k = (H2(k) - 1/2, H3(k) - 1/2) pixel
stages.concepts: sampling, aliasing, supersampling over time, low-discrepancy sequences

stages.title: Final frame + thermal / computer vision
stages.caption: The finished frame, and the same world through the UAV's thermal sensor: heat instead of light, sensor noise and the computer-vision stage on top: Otsu threshold, connected components, blob classes.
stages.formula: t = max(floor, Otsu + 1)       blob = 8-connected component of (heat >= t)
